author: LOLITA C. BALDOR
title: Review of U.S. Troop Deployment at Guantanamo Bay
text:
• Military officials are reviewing plans to cut the number of U.S. troops at Guantanamo Bay by up to half.
• Currently, there are 900 troops deployed at the base.
• There are no detainees at Guantanamo Bay as of now, with the last 40 detainees flown to Louisiana on March 11.
• The military's Southern Command has been asked to outline troop needs and additional space requirements for potential future detainees.
• At least 290 detainees have been transferred to Guantanamo since February.
• The base is known for housing individuals associated with the September 11 attacks and has facilities for migrants intercepted at sea.
• Civil rights attorneys have raised concerns about the transfer of migrants to Guantanamo, claiming many do not have criminal records.
• A recent judge's ruling against immigration advocates was based on the absence of current migrant detainees at the base.
• The current troop composition includes approximately 500 Army soldiers, nearly 300 Marines, and several dozen sailors and airmen.
• Nearly 800 additional U.S.-based soldiers are on prepare-to-deploy orders for potential deployment to Guantanamo.
• The first military transport flight for migrants to Guantanamo occurred on February 4, starting with Venezuelans.
